subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw keep gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback as a documented break-glass mode, or remove/harden it because of DNS-rebinding and CSRF risk?
rationale: The code path is intentional and audited as dangerous, so changing it affects both the gateway security boundary and compatibility for operators who selected the documented fallback.

options.title: Harden The Fallback
options.body: Keep the break-glass flag but require additional browser-request defenses such as Sec-Fetch-Site or a CSRF token plus focused HTTP/WebSocket regression tests.

options.title: Remove The Fallback
options.body: Delete the dangerous mode and provide compatibility handling or doctor guidance for existing configs that rely on it.

options.title: Accept Current Dangerous Mode
options.body: Explicitly document that the audited critical warning is the intended boundary and close this only if maintainers accept the residual DNS-rebinding risk.

recommendation.title: Harden The Fallback
recommendation.body: Keep the break-glass flag but require additional browser-request defenses such as Sec-Fetch-Site or a CSRF token plus focused HTTP/WebSocket regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently landed the related trusted-proxy HTTP origin hardening in this gateway auth surface.
